evidence_refs.quote: a specialised system designed to run transformer-based artificial intelligence models more efficiently
Low Voltage Inference (LVI) is a new paradigm in AI computing that unlocks dramatically better power and cost efficiency.
Cluster Scale Memory (CSM) is a hybrid SRAM/HBM memory subsystem designed around an entire cluster rather than a single chip.
The first, which the company calls Low Voltage Inference, runs the chip's math blocks at under half the voltage of conventional AI chips.
The second innovation, Cluster Scale Memory, creates a shared, low-latency memory pool across chips in the scale-up domain using a proprietary high-bandwidth interconnect.
At the centre of that effort is Sohu, Etched’s custom AI accelerator.
Working with TSMC, Etched has developed a technology it calls low-voltage inference, essentially running the chips at lower voltage to prevent overheating.

The company also developed a memory system that combines two different kinds — the High-Bandwidth Memory that’s critical to Nvidia’s chips and the Static Random-Access Memory that’s increasingly being used in chips meant for fast responses to AI queries.
